about: Both Buttons Pressed is the happy ending to the Daily Struggle comic. In the top panel a gloved hand stretches its thumb and middle finger wide to hit two red buttons on a control panel at the same time; in the bottom panel the same red-shirted man who usually sweats over the choice gives a smug thumbs-up and a satisfied smirk. Where the original is about agonizing between two incompatible options, this version is about refusing to choose at all and doing both, whether that is genuinely clever or obviously a terrible idea. The confident grin makes it read as a flex either way.
origin: It is a follow-up edit of Jake Clark's 2014 two-buttons comic, drawn in the same style and credited on the image to the artist Petirep alongside Clark's Tumblr. It circulates as the answer to the original dilemma.
usage:
Each box labels one button: put two things that seem to rule each other out on them ("fix the bug", "add a feature"). The image itself shows the punchline, so the labels only need to make the contradiction clear.

It works for people who want it both ways: eating salad and dessert, being on a diet and ordering pizza, cheering for both teams, saying you'll sleep early and starting a new series. You can also use it sincerely for a smart compromise, but the smirk lands best when doing both is obviously chaotic.
